questions.stem: The density $\rho$ of a uniform cylinder is determined by measuring its mass m, length l and diameter d. The measured values of m, l and d are $97.42 \pm 0.02$ g, $8.35 \pm 0.05$ mm and $20.20 \pm 0.02$ mm, respectively. Calculated percentage fractional error in $\rho$ is _________.
questions.solution:
$\rho = \frac{m}{\pi\frac{d^{2}}{4}l} = \frac{4m}{\pi d^{2}l}$
$\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\frac{\Delta d}{d} + \frac{\Delta d}{l}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho} = \frac{0.02}{97.42} + \left(\frac{0.02}{20.20} \times 2\right) + \left(\frac{0.05}{8.35}\right)$
$= 0.82\%$

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle changes with distance x from a fixed origin as $V = \frac{A\sqrt{x}}{x + B}$, where A and B are constant with appropriate dimensions. The dimensions of AB are ________.

The rain drop of mass 1 g , starts with zero velocity from a height of 1 km . It hits the ground with a speed of 5 m/s. The work done by the unknown resistive force is __________ J.
(take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
Using work energy theorem
$mgh + W_{res} = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2} - \frac{1}{2}m(0)^{2}$
$\Rightarrow (1 \times 10^{-3})(10)(10^{3}) + W_{res} = \frac{1}{2}(1 \times 10^{-3})(5)^{2} - 0$
$\Rightarrow W_{res} = 0.0125 - 10$
$= -9.9875$ J

questions.stem:
Two blocks (P and Q) with respectively masses 2 kg and 1.5 kg are joined by a massless thread. These blocks are mounted on a frictionless pully which is fixed on the edge of a cube (S), as shown in the figure below. Block P is positioned on the top surface which has no friction and block Q is in contact with side-surface, having coefficient friction $\mu$. The cube (S) moves towards the right with acceleration of $\frac{g}{2}$, where g is gravitational acceleration. During this movement the block P and Q remain stationary. The value of $\mu$ is _______.
(take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
Solving with respect to cube [Both blocks are at rest with respect to cube]
(Figure: FBD of P — $N_{1}$ up, 2g down, T to the right, pseudo force $2(g/2)$ to the left)
$N_{1} = 2g = 20$ N
$T = 2(g/2) = 10$ N
(Figure: FBD of Q — T and $\mu N_{2}$ up, 1.5g down, $N_{2}$ to the right, pseudo force $1.5(g/2)$ to the left)
$\therefore N_{2} = 1.5(g/2) = 7.5$ N
$1.5g = T + \mu N_{2}$
$\Rightarrow 15 = 10 + \mu(7.5)$
$\Rightarrow \mu = \frac{5}{7.5} = \frac{2}{3} = 0.67$

questions.stem:
A lift of mass 1600 kg is supported by thick iron wire. If the maximum stress which the wire can withstand is $4 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{N/m^{2}}$ and its radius is 4 mm , then maximum acceleration the lift can take is ________ $\mathrm{m/s^{2}}$.
(take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$ and $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
(Figure: block m with tension T upward, mg downward, acceleration a upward)
$\therefore T - mg = ma$
$\Rightarrow T = m(g + a)$
$\therefore$ Breaking stree $(\sigma) = \frac{F}{A}$
here F = T
$\Rightarrow \sigma = \frac{T}{A}$
$\Rightarrow T = \sigma A$
$\Rightarrow m(g + a) = \sigma A$
$\Rightarrow a = \frac{\sigma A}{m} - g = \frac{(4 \times 10^{8})(\pi(4 \times 10^{-3})^{2})}{1600} - 10$
$= 2.56\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$

questions.stem: A solid sphere of radius 4 cm and mass 5 kg is rotating (rotation axis is passing through the centre of the sphere) with an angular velocity of 1200 rpm . It is brought to rest in 10 s by applying a constant torque. The torque applied and the number of rotations it made before it comes to rest are _______ and ________ respectively.
questions.solution:
$\because \omega = \omega_{0} + \alpha t$
$0 = \left(1200 \times \frac{2\pi}{60}\right) + \alpha(10)$ $\quad \left[\because 1\mathrm{rpm} = \frac{2\pi}{60}\mathrm{rad}\right]$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = -4\pi\ \mathrm{rad/sec^{2}}$
$\because I = \frac{2}{5}mR^{2} = \frac{2}{5}(5)(4 \times 10^{-2})^{2}$
$\Rightarrow I = 32 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{kgm^{2}}$
$\therefore$ Torque $\tau = I\alpha$
$= -(32 \times 10^{-4})(4\pi)$ Nm
$= -0.0128\pi$ Nm
$\because 0 = \left(\frac{\omega_{0} + \omega}{2}\right)t$
$= \left(\frac{0 + 1200}{20}\right)\left(\frac{10}{60}\right) = 100\mathrm{rot}$ $\quad \left[\because 10\sec = \frac{10}{60}\min\right]$

questions.stem: A smooth inclined plane ends in a vertical circular loop, as shown in the figure. A small body is released from height h as shown. If the body exerts a force of three times its weight on the plane at the highest point of circle then the height $h = \alpha R$. The value of $\alpha$ is _________.
questions.solution:
(Figure: at the top of the loop, velocity $v$ horizontal, $N_{1}$ and mg downward)
$\because N_{1} + mg = \frac{mv_{1}^{2}}{R}$
$3mg + mg = \frac{mv_{1}^{2}}{R}$
$\Rightarrow v_{1}^{2} = 4gR$
Using mechanical energy conservation b/w top of inclined plane and top of circular part.
$mgh + 0 = \frac{1}{2}mv_{1}^{2} + mgR$
$mgh = \frac{m}{2}(4gR) + mgR$
$\Rightarrow h = 3R$

questions.stem: The position of center of mass of three masses 2 kg, 3 kg and 15 kg placed with respect to mid point (p) of normal bisector, as shown in the figure is _________.
questions.solution:
(Figure: altitude $= 10\cos 60^\circ = 5$ m, half-base $= 10\sin 60^\circ = 5\sqrt{3}$ m; with origin at P: 15 kg at (0, 2.5) m, masses at $(-5\sqrt{3}, -2.5)$ m and $(5\sqrt{3}, -2.5)$ m)
$\vec{r}_{cm} = \frac{m_{1}\vec{r}_{1} + m_{2}\vec{r}_{2} + m_{3}\vec{r}_{3}}{m_{1} + m_{2} + m_{3}}$
$= \frac{15(2.5\hat{j}) + 3(5\sqrt{3}\hat{i} - 2.5\hat{j}) + 2(-5\sqrt{3}\hat{i} - 2.5\hat{j})}{15 + 3 + 2}$
$= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\hat{i} + 1.25\hat{j}$

questions.stem: The two wires A and B of equal cross-section but of different materials are joined together. The ratio of Young's modulus of wire A and wire B is 20/11. When the joined wire is kept under certain tension the elongations in the wires A and B are equal. If the length of wire A is 2.2 m , then the length of wire B is _________ m .
questions.solution:
Given that $\frac{Y_{A}}{Y_{B}} = \frac{20}{11}, \frac{A_{A}}{A_{B}} = 1, \frac{\Delta L_{A}}{\Delta L_{B}} = 1, L_{A} = 2.2\mathrm{m}$
When both are joined under certain tension, $T_{A} = T_{B}$
$\Delta L_{A} = \Delta L_{B}$
$\frac{T_{A}L_{A}}{A_{A}Y_{A}} = \frac{T_{B}L_{B}}{A_{B}Y_{B}}$
$\Rightarrow L_{B} = \left(\frac{T_{A}}{T_{B}}\right)\left(\frac{A_{B}}{A_{A}}\right)\left(\frac{Y_{B}}{Y_{A}}\right)L_{A}$
$= (1)(1)\left(\frac{11}{20}\right)(2.2) = 1.21\mathrm{m}$

questions.stem: Two closed vessels of same volume are joined through a narrow tube and both vessels are filled with air of pressure 90 kPa and temperature 400 K . Keeping the temperature of one vessel constant at 400 K the second vessel temperature is raised to 500 K . The final pressure in the vessels is _______ kPa .
questions.solution:
Since total no. of moles will be constant.
$(n_{1} + n_{2})_{i} = (n_{1} + n_{2})_{f}$
$\left[\because n = \frac{PV}{RT}\right]$
$\frac{90V}{R(400)} + \frac{90V}{R(400)} = \frac{P_{f}V}{R(400)} + \frac{P_{f}V}{R(500)}$
$\Rightarrow P_{f} = 100$ kPa

questions.stem: In interference experiment the path difference between two interfering waves at a point A on the screen is $\lambda/3$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of these waves, and at another point B the path difference is $\lambda/6$. The ratio of intensities at points A and B is __________.
questions.solution:
$\because \Delta\phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x$ $\quad$ Considering $I_{1} = I_{2} = I$
At point A,
$\Delta\phi_{A} = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\left(\frac{\lambda}{3}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}$
$I_{A} = I_{1} + I_{2} + 2\sqrt{I_{1}I_{2}}\cos(\Delta\phi_{A})$
$= I + I + 2\sqrt{II}\cos(2\pi/3)$
$I_{A} = I$
At point B,
$\Delta\phi_{B} = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\left(\frac{\lambda}{6}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}$
$I_{B} = I + I + 2\sqrt{II}\cos(\pi/3)$
$= 3I$
$I_{A}/I_{B} = 1/3$

questions.stem: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion. Its amplitude is A and time period is 5 sec . The time required by it to move from x = A to $x = \frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$ is _________ sec.
questions.solution:
(Figure: phasor circle of radius A; the phasor turns through $\theta$ from x = A to the projection $x = A/\sqrt{2}$)
Using phasor
$\cos\theta = \frac{A/\sqrt{2}}{A}$
$\Rightarrow \theta = \frac{\pi}{4}$
$\because \theta = \omega t$
$\frac{\pi}{4} = \left(\frac{2\pi}{T}\right)t \Rightarrow t = \frac{T}{8} = 5/8\sec$

questions.stem:
A thin half ring of radius 35 cm is uniformly charged with a total charge of Q coulomb. If the magnitude of the electric field at centre of the half ring is 100 V/m, then the value of Q is ___________ nC .
$(\epsilon_{0} = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{C^{2}/Nm^{2}}$ and $\pi = 3.14)$
questions.solution:
(Figure: half ring of radius R with linear charge density $\lambda$; field at centre along the symmetry axis)
Electric field $E = \frac{2k\lambda}{R}$
Here $\lambda = \frac{Q}{l} = \frac{Q}{\pi R}$
So $E = \frac{2kQ}{\pi R^{2}}$
$100 = \frac{2(9 \times 10^{9})(Q)}{(3.14)(35 \times 10^{-2})^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow Q = 2.14 \times 10^{-9}$ C

questions.stem:
The maximum rated power of the LED is 2 mW and it is used in the circuit with input voltage of 5 V as shown in the figure below. The current through resistance $R_{S}$ is 0.5 mA.
The minimum value of the resistance of $R_{S}$, to ensure that the LED is not damaged is ________ $\mathrm{k\Omega}$.
questions.solution:
We have to keep the value of $R_{S}$ such that even if whole current of battery passes through the LED, it doesn't get damaged.
Power of LED = iV
$2 \times 10^{-3} = i(V)$
$\Rightarrow 2 \times 10^{-3} = (0.5 \times 10^{-3})V$
$\Rightarrow V = 4$ volt
(Figure: potential 5 V before $R_{S}$ (current 0.5 mA), 4 V after it across both branches, 0 V at the bottom rail)
$R_{S} = \frac{5 - 4}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}}$
$R_{S} = 2000\ \Omega$
$\Rightarrow R_{S} = 2\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$

questions.stem: A point light source emits E.M. waves in free space. A detector, placed at a distance of L m, measures the intensity as $I_{0}$. The detector is now shifted to another location on the same spherical surface ensuring the angle between original location and new location as $45^\circ$. The measured intensity at new location will be __________.
questions.solution:
(Figure: point source at centre of a sphere of radius R; points A and B on it separated by $45^\circ$)
$\because$ Intensity $I = \frac{\mathrm{Power}(P)}{4\pi R^{2}}$
& It will be same at both points A and B.

questions.stem: A spherical interface lens of radius R separates two media of refractive indices 1 and 1.4 respectively as shown in the figure below. A point source is placed at a distance of 4R in front of spherical interface. The magnitude of the magnification of point source image is ________ .
questions.solution:
(Figure: sign convention — negative to the left, positive to the right of the surface)
$u = -4R, R = +R, n_{i} = 1, n_{r} = 1.4$
$\because \frac{n_{r}}{v} - \frac{n_{i}}{u} = \frac{n_{r} - n_{i}}{R}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1.4}{v} - \frac{1}{(-4R)} = \frac{1.4 - 1}{R}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1.4}{v} + \frac{1}{4R} = \frac{4}{10R}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1.4}{v} = \frac{4}{10R} - \frac{1}{4R} = \frac{6}{40R}$
$\Rightarrow v = \frac{40R(1.4)}{60} = \frac{56R}{6}$
Magnification $m = \frac{\left(\frac{v}{n_{r}}\right)}{\left(\frac{u}{n_{i}}\right)} = \frac{v}{u} \times \frac{n_{i}}{n_{r}}$
$= \left(\frac{56R}{6}\right)\left(\frac{1}{-4R}\right) \times \frac{1}{1.4}$
$= -1.66$

questions.stem:
A small cube of side 1 mm is placed at the centre of a circular loop of radius 10 cm carrying a current of 2 A . The magnetic energy stored inside the cube is $\alpha \times 10^{-14}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ______ .
$(\mu_{o} = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \mathrm{Tm/A}, \pi = 3.14)$
questions.solution:
Magnetic energy = (energy density) volume
$= \left(\frac{B^{2}}{2\mu_{0}}\right)(a^{3})$
$\because B = \frac{\mu_{0}i}{2R} = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7})(2)}{2(10 \times 10^{-2})}$ T
$B = 4\pi \times 10^{-6}$ T
$a = 1\mathrm{mm} = 1 \times 10^{-3}$
So magnetic energy
$= \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-6})^{2}}{2(4\pi \times 10^{-7})}(1 \times 10^{-3})^{3}$
$= 6.28 \times 10^{-14}$ J

questions.stem: An inductor of inductance 10 mH having resistance of $100\ \Omega$ is connected to battery of E.M.F. 1.0 V through a switch as shown in the figure below. After switch is closed, the ratio of instantaneous voltages across the inductor when the current passing through it is 2 mA and 4 mA is _________ .
questions.solution:
(Figure: series loop of L, R and cell $\varepsilon$ with current i; $V_{A}$ between L and R, $V_{B}$ at both ends)
voltage across inductor is $V_{A} - V_{B} = \varepsilon - iR$
Ratio of voltages $= \frac{\varepsilon - i_{1}R}{\varepsilon - i_{2}R}$
$= \frac{(1) - (2 \times 10^{-3})(100)}{1 - (4 \times 10^{-3})(100)}$
$= \frac{0.8}{0.6} = 4/3$

questions.stem: The ratio of momentum of the photons of the $1^{st}$ and $2^{nd}$ line of Balmer series of Hydrogen atoms is $\alpha/\beta$. The possible values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are :
questions.solution:
$\because \frac{1}{\lambda} = Rz^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right)$
and momentum of photon $p = \frac{h}{\lambda}$
So $p = \frac{h}{\lambda} = Rhz^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right)$
For $1^{st}$ line of polmer series
$n_{1} = 2, n_{2} = 3$
For $2^{nd}$ line of polmer series
$n_{1} = 2, n_{2} = 4$
$\frac{p_{1}}{p_{2}} = \frac{Rhz^{2}\left(\frac{1}{2^{2}} - \frac{1}{3^{2}}\right)}{Rhz^{2}\left(\frac{1}{2^{2}} - \frac{1}{4^{2}}\right)}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{p_{1}}{p_{2}} = \left(\frac{5}{36}\right) \times \left(\frac{16}{3}\right) = \frac{20}{27} = \frac{\alpha}{\beta}$
$\alpha = 20, \beta = 27$

questions.stem: A LCR series circuit driven with $E_{rms} = 90$ V at frequency $f_{d} = 30$ Hz has resistance $R = 80\ \Omega$, an inductance with inductive reactance $X_{L} = 20.0\ \Omega$ and capacitance with capacitive reactance $X_{C} = 80.0\ \Omega$. The power factor of the circuit is _________.
Refer to the circuit diagram given below. The heat generated across the $6\ \Omega$ resistance in 100 second is $\frac{\alpha}{100}$ J . The value of $\alpha$ is _______. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
(Figure: taking the right-hand junction as 0 V, the left end is at 2 V, the junction x joins $3\Omega$, $4\Omega$ and the $6\Omega$ branch whose cell end is at 3 V)
Net outgoing current is zero from x
$\frac{x - 2}{3} + \frac{x - 0}{4} + \frac{x - 3}{6} = 0$
$\Rightarrow 4x - 8 + 3x + 2x - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \frac{14}{9}$ V
Potenteal difference across $6\Omega$ is $\left(3 - \frac{14}{9}\right)V = \frac{13}{9}V$
So heat generated $H = \frac{V^{2}}{R}t$
$H = \left(\frac{13}{9}\right)^{2}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)(100) = \frac{\alpha}{100}$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 3477$

questions.stem: An unpolarized light of intensity $I_{0}$ passes through polarizer and then through a certain optically active solution and finally it goes to analyser. If the angle between analyser and polariser is $0^\circ$ and intensity of light emerged from analyser is $\frac{3}{8}I_{0}$, the angle of rotation of the light by the solution with respect to analyser is ________ degrees.
questions.solution:
(Figure: $I_{0}$ → polarizer → $\frac{I_{0}}{2}$ → analyzer at angle $\theta$ → $\frac{I_{0}}{2}\cos^{2}\theta$)
Given that
$\frac{I_{0}}{2}\cos^{2}\theta = \frac{3I_{0}}{8}$
$\Rightarrow \cos\theta = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ$

questions.stem:
The energy released when $\frac{7}{17.13}$ kg of $\mathrm{^{7}_{3}Li}$ is converted into $\mathrm{^{4}_{2}He}$ by proton bombardment is $\alpha \times 10^{32}$ eV. The value of $\alpha$ is _________ . (Nearest integer)
(Mass of $\mathrm{^{7}_{3}Li} = 7.0183$u, mass of $\mathrm{^{4}_{2}He} = 4.004$u, mass of proton $= 1.008$u and $1\mathrm{u} = 931\ \mathrm{MeV/c^{2}}$ and Avogadro number $= 6.0 \times 10^{23}$)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{^{7}_{3}Li} + \mathrm{proton} \rightarrow 2\,\mathrm{^{4}_{2}He}$
Energy released for one lithium atom is Q
$\Rightarrow Q = (\Delta m)c^{2}$
$= (m_{Li} + m_{proton} - 2m_{He})c^{2}$
$= [7.0183 + 1.008 - 2(4.004)]931\mathrm{MeV}$
$Q = (17.031 \times 10^{6}\ \mathrm{eV})$
Total no. of lithium atoms
$= \frac{7}{17.13} \times \frac{1}{7 \times 10^{-3}} \times 6 \times 10^{23}$
$= \frac{6 \times 10^{23}}{17.13}$
So total energy released
$(17.037 \times 10^{6})\left(\frac{6}{17.13} \times 10^{26}\right)$ eV
$= 5.96 \times 10^{26}$ eV

questions.stem: A three coulomb charge moves from the point (0, $-2$, $-5$) to the point (5, 1, 2) in an electric field expressed as $\vec{E} = 2x\hat{i} + 3y^{2}\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\ \mathrm{N/C}$. The work done in moving the charge is _______ J.

A certain gas is isothermally compressed to $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{rd}$ of its initial volume ($V_{0} = 3$ litre) by applying required pressure. If the bulk modulus of the gas is $3 \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{N/m^{2}}$, the magnitude of work done on the gas is ______ J.
questions.solution:
Work done by gas in isothermal process is
$W = nRT\ln\left(\frac{V_{F}}{V_{i}}\right)$ or $P_{i}V_{i}\ln\left(\frac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}\right)$
$\because P_{i}$ = Bulk modulus (for isothermal process)
$= 3 \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{N/m^{2}}$
$V_{i} = 3$ ltr $= 3 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^{3}}$
$V_{f} = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)V_{i} = 1\mathrm{ltr} = 1 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^{3}}$
So $W = (3 \times 10^{5})(3 \times 10^{-3})\ln\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)$
$= -900\ln(3) = -900(1.0986)$
$= -988.74$ J
As asked in question, work done on the gas is negative of work done by the gas so that will be equal to 988.74 J
So Answer is 989 J (Closest integer)
